newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Nov 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government's plans to sell its interest in the heavily subsidised Australian National Rail Corp in a A$2 billion package within the next 12 months will blow out the bottom line of the 1996-97 budget. Page 1.

Seventeen of the 18 APEC member nations have offered to cut tariffs beyond their existing commitments at the APEC annual summit in Manila in what Prime Minister John Howard has described as the point where "the rubber hits the road" in market-opening. Page 1.

Major superannuation services and consultant group Towers Perrin has expressed grave concerns about the government's surcharge proposals in a submission to Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, claiming the super surcharge won't work, failing to raise the A$50 million revenue target and imposing costs up to A$70 million on the industry. Page 3.

An application by the State Public Services Federation of Victoria for a federal paid rates award will be opposed by the federal government at a hearing before the industrial Relations Commission. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Signalling a new era in U.S.-Sino relations, an announcement came yesterday that U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin had agreed on two summits in Washington and Beijing at the same time as Prime Minister John Howard met with the Chinese leader to dispel any doubts about Australia's relationship with China. On the eve of today's APEC leaders summit in the Philippines, Howard accepted an invitation to visit Beijing next year. Page 1.

Starting the day with a four-shot lead, Greg Norman left his rivals for dead yesterday to win his fifth Australian Open golf championship at the Jack Nicklaus-designed course in Sydney. Norman was the only player to finish under par, beating fellow Queenlander Wayne Grady by eight shots and taking away A$180,000 first prize money and what is understood to be a A$250,000 appearance fee. Page 1.

Despite a promise by Federal Transport Minister John Sharp that his A$2 billion package to privatise the Australian National rail network would lead to a "renaissance of rail", New South Wales Premier Bob Carr had other ideas yesterday when he threatened to veto the planned privatisation of interstate freight services. Under the proposal, three of Australia's prestige railway services, the Ghan, the Indian-Pacific and the Overlander, would be sold, as would railway workshops in South Australia and Tasmania. Page 1.

In a Senate committee report into the limiting of Medicare provider numbers, to be tabled in Federal Parliament today, the West Australian and New South Wales governments have urged the federal government to review its restriction on the number of doctors entering general practice, claiming the move would compound existing doctor shortages. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the lead up to the APEC leaders summit in the Philippines, Prime Minister John Howard has foreshadowed a new relationship with China after meeting Chinese President Jiang Zemin yesterday. In other APEC developments, Australia has backed down in a trade dispute with the U.S. over export incentive schemes and the federal government has indicated it plans to wind back some of Australia's foreign investment restrictions by mid-1997. Page 1.

Following a year-long investigation of school performance, the New South Wales Department of School education will today release a list of 256 of the state's top high schools, based on a complex new system of tracing students' performance from Year 7 to HC level. Parent and teacher groups have been opposed to the release of the information, but the Carr government intends to continue with its push to provide parents with more information about performance. Page 1.

Federal Industrial relations Minister Peter Reith will today release a discussion paper which proposes radical reforms to the public service, including placing senior bureaucrats on contract, abandoning costly hire and fire procedures, emphasising productvity trade-offs in pay negotiations, and requiring agency heads to abide by "public performance agreements". Page 3.

Flash floods in the New South Wales North Coast town of Coffs Harbour damaged more than 300 businesses and homes and led to the death of 53-year-old Alannah Amanda on the weekend after she hit her head and was washed out to sea. Three people are still missing after an estimated 30 centimetres of rain fell in two hours. Page 3.
THE AGE

A report to be released today by the Human Rights and Equal Opportunities Commission has revealed the A$30 million Royal Commission into Black Deaths in Custody has failed to reduce the death rate among Aborigines in jail, with 96 dead since the beginning of the Royal Commission in June 1989. Page A1.

Five armed men breached security at the Toorak mansion owned by property tycoon John Gandel on Saturday night, abducting a caretaker and holding him at gunpoint until he convinced them he was not a member of the Gandel family. None of the Gandel family were home at the time. Page A1.

China has signalled a decision to back away from its aggressive relations with the U.S. and Australia after assurances by U.S. President Bill Clinton and Prime Minister John Howard in Manila yesterday that their countries sought friendship with China, not containment. Page A1.

Australia's passenger rail services, the Indian-Pacific, Ghan and Overlander, will be sold under a A$2 billion federal government plan to privatise the debt-laden Australian National railway. The Commonwealth will also sell its 40 percent stake in the Naional Rail Corporation, which is part-owned by the Victorian and New South Wales governments. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
